title: Dispatch: Supervisor self-review round 2 findings on PR #524 head 97b2ff0
description:
Supervisor self-review round 2 of PR #524 head 97b2ff0. Round 1's eight findings are all confirmed fixed (8 of 60 tests fail against 7199f7a; full verification 276 files / 4868 tests). Round-2 probes of the new position-authority surfaces found no holes — the ordinal-0 bootstrap closes once real chronology exists, and stale AND future currentPosition assertions are both rejected.

SEVEN new findings. Four of them (1, 2, 3, 6) are consequences of round 1's own fixes, which is why this loop exists. All are accepted; none was rejected this round.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev5 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev5, cut from eshyra-jhpt at 97b2ff0. Run `npm ci` before verification.

=============================================================
FINDING 1 (blocking) — a disputed turn cannot be corrected by SUPERSESSION, only by adding a competing rule.
=============================================================
campaignRuleStore.ts supersedeCampaignRule rejects any successor whose effectivePosition precedes currentPosition, unconditionally. But checkTemporalMode explicitly PERMITS a disputed-turn position at the immediately preceding turn, and createCampaignRule accepts exactly that. So the one operation a disputed turn most needs — replacing the rule that produced the bad adjudication — is the one that is forbidden.
REPRODUCED at 97b2ff0 (supervisor): r1 prospective at turn 1, advance to turn 2, supersede r1 with a disputed-turn successor anchored at turn 1 ->
    "successor 'r2' cannot take effect before the current position"
Consequence: the correction can only be authored as a NEW rule, the prior rule stays active, and both apply at the disputed turn — which is precisely the contradictory-active-rules state this branch has been closing elsewhere. eshyra-jhpt.8 depends on this path.
FIX: the guard must carry the same temporalMode condition checkTemporalMode uses — only a PROSPECTIVE successor must be at or after the current position; a disputed-turn successor is bounded by the disputed-turn rules instead. Test that a disputed-turn supersession at the immediately preceding turn succeeds, that the prior rule stops being active at the disputed position, and that an OLDER disputed target is still rejected.

=============================================================
FINDING 2 (blocking) — the disputed-turn anchor is never validated against persisted chronology.
=============================================================
Round 1 made currentPosition authoritative by checking it against campaign_turn_position (assertCurrentPosition). disputedPosition got no such treatment. checkTemporalMode's immediatelyBefore accepts on sessionId + ordinal + 1 alone, so the turnId is unchecked.
REPRODUCED at 97b2ff0 (supervisor): real turn 1 is 'aaa-turn'; current turn 2 is 'zzz-turn'. A caller reusing the CURRENT turn id with the PREVIOUS ordinal — an easy and realistic mistake — creates { s1, 'zzz-turn', ordinal 1 }, which is ACCEPTED. Then:
    active at the REAL disputed turn: []      <- the correction is not there
The rule exists, is active, and is silently never in force at the turn it was created to correct. Whether it appears at all depends on lexicographic comparison of two turn ids.
FIX: validate disputedPosition against the persisted campaign_turn_position row for that ordinal, the same way assertCurrentPosition validates currentPosition. The store already has getCurrentCampaignPosition and the table; add the lookup it needs rather than trusting the caller. Keep the domain-level checkTemporalMode as-is for pure-domain use, but the STORE must not admit a fabricated anchor.

=============================================================
FINDING 3 (blocking) — the comparator comment I asked for in round 1 asserts something false, and the divergence is reachable.
=============================================================
campaignRules.ts:312 and campaignRuleStore.ts:490 now justify SQL BINARY comparison with "Equal ordinals cannot be persisted for one campaign". That uniqueness constraint exists only on campaign_turn_position. campaign_rule.effective_position and revoked_position are caller-supplied and unconstrained, so equal-ordinal/different-anchor rows ARE reachable — finding 2 is one route to them.
On such a tie, SQL compares the percent-ENCODED sessionId~turnId while compareCampaignPositions compares the DECODED values, and they disagree whenever encodeURIComponent escapes a character ('a b' -> 'a%20b' sorts after 'a!b' encoded, before it decoded). assertNoOverlappingAmbiguityRuling / intervalsOverlap and the active-at-position query can then reach opposite conclusions about the same pair.
FIX: a comment is no longer sufficient — round 1 tried that and the comment is wrong. Make the two orderings genuinely one. Either compare the canonical encoded form on both sides, or stop relying on BINARY SQL ordering where a tie is possible. Then correct or delete the false justification at both sites. Test an equal-ordinal pair whose encoded and decoded orders differ, and assert the SQL predicate and the JS comparator agree.

=============================================================
FINDING 4 — overlap check runs before the duplicate-identity check, so a duplicate reports a nonexistent conflict.
=============================================================
campaignRuleStore.ts writeRule runs assertNoOverlappingAmbiguityRuling before the existence check, so re-creating an existing ambiguity ruling compares the row against ITSELF: "active ambiguity ruling 'r1' overlaps 'r1' for ambiguity 'ambiguity:x'" instead of "campaign rule 'r1' already exists". A caller — or a tool retry path — will hunt a conflicting ruling that does not exist.
FIX: move the existence check above the overlap check. Test that a duplicate create reports the duplicate, not an overlap.

=============================================================
FINDING 5 — a player-approved ruling silently vanishes from DM context if its ambiguity leaves the bound pack.
=============================================================
campaignContext.ts excludes ambiguity rulings from `rules` and re-attaches them only by matching ambiguities present in the currently bound rules stack. If the campaign rebinds to a pack revision where that ambiguity id no longer exists, the still-active, player-approved ruling is fetched by nothing and rendered nowhere — no trace, no loss record — while listCampaignRules still reports it active.
This is the silent-disappearance class the epic exists to prevent; the DM would adjudicate as if the table had never ruled.
FIX: an active ruling whose ambiguity is not in the bound stack must not vanish silently. Surface it (with its provenance, noting the ambiguity is absent from the current pack) or record an explicit loss the caller can see. Decide which and say why. Test it by binding a stack without the ambiguity and asserting the ruling is still accounted for.

=============================================================
FINDING 6 — round 1's finding-7 fix made the trace under-report the query that ran.
=============================================================
campaignRuleSeam.ts passes includeAllActive: options.rulingsOnly !== true, so the first join's ambiguityIds argument is now dead — the seam returns every active ambiguity ruling regardless of what was asked. But the trace still reports requestedAmbiguityIds as the candidate-derived list, directly contradicting the comment twenty lines above it: "Request evidence is derived from the calls that ACTUALLY executed, never from what this stage could have asked."
Concretely, measurements.ts m5.returned can contain ruling identities for ambiguities absent from m5.requestedAmbiguityIds, and m5.unqueriedAmbiguityIds is computed from that under-reported offered set, so the trace no longer describes the query that ran. That trace is transition-measurement evidence (M5), so its truthfulness is load-bearing.
FIX: make the trace describe the call that actually executed. If the first join asks for all active rulings, say so in the request evidence rather than reporting a candidate-derived list it did not use. Keep the comment's rule true.

=============================================================
FINDING 7 — the new prompt section is not registered, so structural debug logging misattributes it.
=============================================================
renderContextMessage now emits a "## Campaign Rules" heading, but debug/sessionDebug.ts KNOWN_PROMPT_SECTION_LABELS was not updated, and its docstring states it is "The fixed set of `## ` headings emitted by ... renderContextMessage". sanitizePromptSectionName therefore collapses this code-owned heading into the "## (content)" placeholder reserved for UNTRUSTED prompt-derived text — so the debug log reports a code-emitted section as unrecognized.
FIX: register "## Campaign Rules". The sweep also found "## Character Chronicle" and "## Adventure Module (DM-only)" already missing for the same reason; fix all three together and note it, since it is one defect with three instances.

GENERAL
  - NEGATIVE PROOF per finding against 97b2ff0; report the counts you actually observed.
  - Do not weaken existing tests or assertions.
  - Do not touch the merged migrations, the position encoding format, or the rejected relevance-selection finding (eshyra-umyb).
  - Keep every round-1 fix intact: persisted-chronology currentPosition authority, single validation channel, sameTurn ordinal equality, CampaignRuleError on duplicate, ambiguity payload validation, single ruling placement.

VERIFICATION
`npm ci` first, then `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing. Report pass/skip counts and confirm worktree-local @eshyra/core resolution.
